title: Conditional Expressions
scenario: Use a conditional expression to choose a bucket name suffix or retention value based on var.environment.

focus.title: Complete the bucket name expression
focus.todo: Use a conditional expression so production keeps the base name and other environments get a suffix.

hints.why: A conditional expression lets one configuration express a small policy difference without duplicating a whole file. That is often the cleanest way to handle environment-specific settings.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_s3_bucket" "this"`. Use a conditional expression so production keeps the base name and other environments get a suffix. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use a conditional when a value has two clear branches. If the branches affect whole resources or many arguments, separate configuration or a module is usually easier to maintain.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_s3_bucket" "this"`. Use this code shape: bucket. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.environment`, `var.bucket_name`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
